22 THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE

with each other. With a desire to provide for the social development of young men and women, it is proper to call attention to the fact that this institution is not a "Young Ladies' Seminary." Parents who wish their daughters to have the advantages of an ideal control which some schools exercise over their pupils could not send their daughters to the University of Texas. Only earnest young women, imbued with a desire to profit by the methods of advanced education would be benefited by the institution. It is proper that young men, should attend an institution where coeducational principles prevail, as it is proper that they should attend other higher institutions of learning, open to males and females on equal terms.²⁷

GROWTH IN ENROLLMENT.—The coeducational policy doubtless served a purpose in furthering the rapid development of Savoy College in the face of its competition, for approximately forty per cent of the student body at any one moment was made up of females. Concurrent enrollment statistics for all years are not available; but those for 1884-1885 show that enrollment was well above two hundred students. Over 250 were reported by 1881; 369 were enrolled in 1880-1884; 375 were enrolled with the increase of pupils, by reason of the years.

The number enrolled by name in the catalog of 1887-1888 (probably the enrollment of the year) show 415 graduates.²⁸
